correctness.rationale: For round RP^2, supporting projective geodesics have period pi; a second random line intersects a fixed one at a uniform phase, and independent arc-phase inclusion gives crossing kernel ell*s/pi^2. Thus degree conditional on fixed length ell is exactly Bin(n-1,mu*ell/pi^2), despite cross-vertex dependency. Short iid lengths with F(t)~ct^alpha give a PPP of n^(1/alpha)L at zero. For alpha>1, b_n=n^(1-1/alpha)->infinity; binomial variances for O(b_n) short degrees yield joint o_P(b_n) errors among tight-many short arcs, and a Chernoff+union bound excludes long arcs from every bounded scaled-degree interval. Continuous mapping yields stated PPP and order-statistic survival. Binomial-mixture Stieltjes regular variation at scale n^-1 yields alpha c Gamma(k+alpha)/k!*(pi^2/(mu*n))^alpha, for every fixed k. Haar-projective endpoints give |u dot v| uniform, F=1-cos t, mu=1 and specialized pi^4 constants. Independently evaluated k=0,1,3 exact binomial mixtures at n=20000; observed ratios ~0.99995 to predicted constants, only finite numerical corroboration.
residual_risks: Alpha>1 is essential to the Chernoff n exp(-a b_n) exclusion; alpha<=1 not addressed.
General law assumes line/phase/length independence and round RP²; shared-endpoint complete graph model is different.

originality.rationale: Acan analyzes uniformly matched circle chords and degree distribution, not independent isotropic projective geodesic arcs with regularly varying lengths. Bonamy–Mohar–Wesolek treat graphon/edge/triangle densities in spherical drawings of complete bipartite graphs with shared endpoints, not short-arc degree extremes on RP². The published geodesic-needle record gives conditional binomial degrees and variance on the sphere; the present theorem uses this idea but establishes a projective length-to-degree PPP and exact fixed-degree lower tail for alpha>1. The projective factor pi^-2 and dependent-degree global minimum analysis are additional exact objects.

value.rationale: Extreme-degree process is a natural global network invariant; its precise scaling and coefficients reflect rare shortest arcs while crossing edges have strong dependence. Proving a full Poisson point-process limit and fixed-k rare-degree probabilities for arbitrary regularly varying short tails is a structural probabilistic result beyond a single conditional expectation or simulation. The failure of the method at alpha<=1 gives a mathematically meaningful regime boundary.
